players.product: AI cluster design/integration & managed services (plus Smart Modular memory)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Kash Shaikh and interim CFO Aaron Johnson: Q4 FY2026 set company records for net sales, gross profit dollars, operating income, operating margin, net income and adjusted EBITDA. Net sales were $567 million, up 68% year-over-year and up 18% sequentially; gross margin was 28.8%, operating margin 15.8%, and diluted EPS was $1, up 133% year-over-year. The AI-driven businesses (non-hyperscale AI infrastructure and Integrated Memory) represented 78% of company net sales and grew 141% year-over-year. After relatively flat year-over-year net sales in the first half, growth accelerated to 48% in Q3 and 68% in Q4, driving second half growth of 58%.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales $567 million, +68% YoY, +18% QoQ; gross margin 28.8%; operating margin 15.8%; EPS $1, +133%; AI-driven businesses 78% of sales, +141% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Aaron Johnson: Q4 gross margin of 28.8% was up 70 basis points sequentially, supported by improved profitability in Integrated Memory, partially offset by lower Advanced Computing margins; record gross profit of $163 million was up 21% sequentially and 57% year-over-year. Q4 operating expenses were $73 million (up 4% sequentially, 13% year-over-year), and record Q4 operating income of $90 million rose 39% sequentially and 129% year-over-year, with operating margin expanding 2.4 percentage points sequentially and 4.2 percentage points year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA was a record $93 million, up 115% year-over-year. Q4 product net sales were $510 million (90% of total), up 86% year-over-year; services net sales were $57 million (10%), down 11% year-over-year, reflecting lower hyperscale services volumes partially offset by growth in multi-year AI factory managed services.
quarterly_data.figure: gross profit $163 million; operating income $90 million, +129% YoY; adjusted EBITDA $93 million; product $510 million, +86%; services $57 million, -11%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Aaron Johnson: full-year FY2026 net sales were $1.73 billion, up 26% versus fiscal 2025, and diluted EPS rose 51% to $2.87, $0.22 above the high end of the July outlook. Full-year gross profit reached a record $508 million; gross margin was 29.3%, down 1.7 percentage points, primarily due to a greater contribution from AI infrastructure hardware even with stronger Integrated Memory margins. Operating expenses rose 4% to $267 million; operating income reached a record $241 million, up 44%, with operating margin expanding 1.7 percentage points to 13.9%; full-year adjusted EBITDA was $256 million, up 37%.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 net sales $1.73 billion, +26%; EPS $2.87, +51%; gross margin 29.3%; operating income $241 million, +44%; adjusted EBITDA $256 million

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced Computing Q4 net sales were $154 million (27% of company net sales), up 11% year-over-year and 12% sequentially; non-hyperscale AI infrastructure net sales grew 99% year-over-year and were 66% of Advanced Computing net sales, up from 60% in the prior-year quarter, more than offsetting continued runoff from other traditional businesses. For the full year Advanced Computing net sales were $559 million, down 14%, reflecting the Penguin Edge wind-down and lower hyperscale hardware sales, while the non-hyperscale AI infrastructure business grew 72% for the year.
quarterly_data.figure: Advanced Computing Q4 $154 million, +11% YoY; non-hyperscale AI infrastructure +99%, 66% of segment; FY $559 million, -14%; non-hyperscale AI infrastructure +72% for the year

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 added six new AI infrastructure customers - four neoclouds, a large quantitative trading firm and an enterprise customer; across fiscal 2026 Penguin added 17 new AI infrastructure customers while 12 customers expanded their business. CEO: bookings accelerated further entering fiscal 2027; land-and-expand includes ClusterWareAI and multi-year managed services engagements that typically span three to five years. CEO on the neocloud surge: Penguin has seen 'a recent surge in interest' from neocloud providers, which he believes reflects strong product-market fit for its full stack platform, serving as a single operating partner across the life cycle so neoclouds can meet service level agreements and focus on securing additional off-takers.
quarterly_data.figure: 6 new AI infrastructure customers in Q4 (4 neoclouds); 17 new AI infrastructure customers and 12 expansions in fiscal 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Neocloud wins named by the CEO (customers unnamed except Lektra): a neocloud backed by a leading South Korean technology company selected Penguin to design, build, deploy and manage an NVIDIA GB300 NVL72-based platform, with the initial deployment expected to support a broader GPU-as-a-service expansion; a publicly traded neocloud provider with more than $3 billion in signed multi-year AI infrastructure contracts selected Penguin for a multi-year engagement providing AI infrastructure deployment and 24/7 operation services supported by ClusterWareAI; Lektra selected the full stack AI factory platform for distributed AI micro data centers; and another neocloud provider with $10 billion in contracted compute from a leading AI lab selected Penguin to deploy and operate a 36,000 GPU AI factory in Norway in a multi-year engagement. In Q&A the CEO said most of these projects 'have already started' - Penguin is managing or building their data centers, with some in procurement - and that some of the work 'accelerated into the bookings recently'.
quarterly_data.figure: neocloud with more than $3 billion in signed contracts; neocloud with $10 billion in contracted compute; 36,000 GPU AI factory in Norway

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog and bookings: in AI infrastructure and Integrated Memory, bookings grew faster than net sales in Q4 and Penguin ended fiscal 2026 with record company backlog, which management describes as strong across both memory and AI infrastructure (it does not disclose how much of the FY2027 outlook is covered). CEO: the Advanced Computing outlook moved from the preliminary mid-teens to 40% because 'we have booked more than we expected'. In memory, the backlog 'is much higher than the revenue that we recognized in this quarter' and 'now extend to at least four quarters, and it continues to strengthen'.
quarterly_data.figure: record company backlog; memory backlog extends to at least four quarters

quarterly_data.signal: Integrated Memory Q4 net sales reached a record $341 million (60% of company net sales), up 158% year-over-year and 24% sequentially, with increases in both volume and pricing; two new memory customer logos were added in Q4, and across fiscal 2026 Penguin added 50 new customers while 29 existing customers expanded their business. Full-year Integrated Memory net sales were $924 million, up 99%, and represented 53% of total company net sales, up from 34% in fiscal 2025. CEO: while memory is a cyclical market, 'we believe AI is adding a structural demand driver, particularly for memory solutions in the data center'; Penguin's focus is primarily on data center solutions, with engineering design, firmware, validation, negotiated pricing and an asset-light model designed to deliver more resilient economics across memory cycles. He added that if agentic AI is adopted in enterprises at 10%, 'for every 10% increase, that demand can double'.
quarterly_data.figure: Integrated Memory Q4 $341 million, +158% YoY, +24% QoQ; FY $924 million, +99%, 53% of sales; 50 new customers in fiscal 2026

quarterly_data.signal: CXL and MemoryAI: CEO says bookings and pipeline for the CXL memory expansion products continue to strengthen - in Q4 Penguin secured business with a leading global AI server manufacturer (unnamed) whose platforms support large-scale AI training and inference, and expanded its relationship with a leading next-generation AI infrastructure inference provider (unnamed) rapidly scaling inference deployments with Penguin's CXL memory expansion cards. The cards are primarily for inference workloads and 'we see this CXL business taking off very strongly'. Penguin is also developing a CXL AIC product line designed to repurpose installed DDR4 memory for AI infrastructure, and its MemoryAI roadmap extends to future memory appliances including photonic high-bandwidth memory solutions to expand GPU memory capacity and bandwidth.

Supply: in Q4 Penguin established a new supply arrangement with a leading memory supplier (unnamed) to support its data center AI infrastructure portfolio and strengthen its supply position, and a relationship with another AI hardware supplier (unnamed) to help expand supply availability. CFO: the FY2027 outlook incorporates current assumptions for memory supply and costs, 'which may evolve during the year', including the expected impact of these new memory and AI infrastructure suppliers; certain components continue to have extended lead times that can affect project and shipment timing. Inventory rose to $749 million from $255 million a year ago (inventory days 48), reflecting purchases to support record backlog and expected deployments plus higher memory costs.
quarterly_data.figure: inventory $749 million (vs $255 million a year ago); inventory days 48

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on neocloud economics and segment margins: unit economics with neocloud customers are 'quite similar' to enterprise on-premise AI factory deployments, with Penguin able to procure and design the hardware, build the data center and manage it day two and beyond for up to three to five years with ClusterWare to meet SLAs. Penguin does not disclose segment margins, but memory 'continues to be strong, stronger than we expected'; as more wins include both hardware and software, AI infrastructure 'may have some downward pressure', offset by a very high attach rate of ClusterWare software and services.

CEO on demand and platform: inference at scale is creating increasingly memory-intensive workloads - GPUs remain critical, but CPUs and conventional memory including DRAM must also scale. Enterprises and AI-native companies primarily consume AI infrastructure from neocloud providers, while large enterprises increasingly consider on-premises AI factories for persistent inference workloads (better token economics, data control and performance), also considering open weight models. The full stack AI factory platform combines ClusterWareAI operating system software, MemoryAI and Integrated Memory, ComputeAI GPU and CPU systems, OriginAI factory architectures, and design, build, deploy and managed services; ClusterWareAI added agentic capabilities including an AI Factory Operations Agent with a natural language interface for administrators.

Optimized LED Q4 net sales were $72 million (13% of company net sales), up 7% year-over-year; full-year net sales were $249 million, down 3%. Management keeps its investment priorities on data center, AI infrastructure and memory while managing LED with discipline.
quarterly_data.figure: LED Q4 $72 million, +7% YoY; FY $249 million, -3%

quarterly_data.signal: Cash flow and operating model: cash used in operating activities was $163 million in Q4 and $152 million for the full year, mainly working capital for the memory and AI infrastructure businesses; net accounts receivable were $796 million and accounts payable $817 million; Penguin ended Q4 with cash and cash equivalents of $647 million. Capital expenditures were $4 million in the quarter and $12 million for the year, and the CFO expects the asset-light model to continue in fiscal 2027. CEO: 95%+ of engineering is in India, memory engineering is in Taiwan and manufacturing is in Malaysia, and the company has capacity to add without expenses rising linearly with revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: operating cash use $163 million in Q4; cash $647 million; capex $12 million for the year
